lines.text: Hi, coders! Today you will write your very first computer program.
By the end of this lesson, you will make a sprite move and talk.
Code is a list of instructions for a computer.
The computer follows the instructions one by one, in order.
It is like making a sandwich: first take the bread, then add the filling, then close it.
This is the Scratch editor. Let us take a tour.
The stage is where your project plays.
Sprites are the characters. You can see them in the sprite list.
The block palette has all the blocks, sorted by colour.
You drag blocks into the code area and snap them together.
Blocks snap together like puzzle pieces.
A stack of blocks is called a script.
When you click the green flag, the script runs from the top to the bottom.
This is Pip the robot. Each square is one step.
Move, move, turn, move. Pip does each block in order.
And Pip reaches the star!
These two scripts use the same blocks.
But on the right, the turn happens too early, so Pip ends up in the wrong place.
When you code, the order of the blocks matters!
Great work! Here are the big ideas.
Now open Scratch and build along, then try the robot puzzles!
